title: e-Tax users may need to re-select electronic notices from September 24
summary: Japan’s e-Tax changes how electronic tax notices are accepted from September 24, 2026. In principle, the old per-filing consent model moves to advance blanket consent in My Page. Even people who previously chose electronic delivery may need to select it again for future notices, while refund notices, tax certificates, mortgage-deduction certificates and invoice-registration notices have specific exceptions.
why_it_matters: This is implementation fine print, not a new tax. The risk is assuming a past e-Tax delivery choice automatically carries forward and then receiving an important notice on paper instead of where you expect it—or overlooking a transition exception that already preserves electronic delivery.

claims.text: From September 24, 2026, e-Tax expands the range of tax notices and administrative dispositions that can be delivered electronically.
claims.basis: National Tax Agency e-Tax implementation notice.

claims.text: The consent method changes in principle from choosing electronic delivery for each application or filing to advance blanket consent in e-Tax My Page.
claims.basis: National Tax Agency states the consent method changes from per-application consent to advance blanket consent.

claims.text: People who previously used electronic delivery generally need to complete the new blanket-consent setting if they want future electronic delivery, subject to listed transition exceptions.
claims.basis: The NTA explicitly warns that even prior electronic-delivery users may need the new setting and gives notice-specific exceptions.

claims.text: Refund-payment notices remain tied to the electronic-delivery choice made on the relevant refund return or application, while electronic application certificates and tax-payment certificates remain available when electronically requested.
claims.basis: Explicit exceptions listed by the NTA.

claims.text: Mortgage-deduction certificates and qualified-invoice registration notices can continue to be delivered electronically based on pre-September-24 consent for qualifying earlier filings or applications.
claims.basis: Transition exceptions stated by the NTA.

claims.text: e-Tax is scheduled to be unavailable from September 19 at 00:00 until September 24 at 08:30, and again for the full day on September 26, because of the national tax-system replacement.

The safest approach for users who rely on e-Tax messages is to verify their My Page delivery setting after September 24 rather than assume an old filing-level preference still controls future notices.
claims.basis: The delivery-consent model changes and the NTA specifically warns prior users about the new selection requirement.

content.key_message: If you rely on e-Tax for tax-office notices, check My Page after September 24 and confirm the new electronic-delivery setting. Past electronic-delivery choices do not universally carry forward.
content.who_is_affected: Individuals, sole proprietors and businesses using e-Tax who want tax-office notices delivered electronically, especially users who previously selected electronic delivery on individual filings or applications.
content.when: The new electronic-notice framework begins September 24, 2026. The new blanket-consent setting becomes available from that date.
content.financial_impact: Usually indirect rather than a new tax cost. Missing or misrouting a tax notice can create avoidable administrative delay, deadline risk or professional-service cost.
content.risk_if_ignored: MED — the main risk is expecting an electronic notice under an old consent choice when the new framework requires a My Page setting, or assuming every notice follows the same rule despite transition exceptions.
content.deadline: No universal filing deadline is created by this change. The practical date is September 24, 2026, when the new setting becomes available.
content.potential_benefit: Keep tax-notice delivery consistent with your preference and reduce the chance of overlooking notices during the system transition.
content.downside: Minimal. Some users do not need to change anything for specific notice types covered by exceptions, so verify the exact notice instead of assuming all e-Tax delivery settings reset.
content.what_would_change_mind: A later National Tax Agency notice that automatically migrates existing users’ preferences more broadly, changes the September 24 start date, or expands the transition exceptions.
content.strongest_counterinterpretation: This is mainly a delivery-setting change, not a tax-law burden. Many taxpayers who only use e-Tax for annual filing may see little immediate effect, and several common notices have explicit exceptions. That limits urgency but does not remove the need for users who depend on electronic notices to verify their setting.
content.what_to_do_or_watch: Do not try to set the new blanket consent before September 24 because the NTA says the function becomes available from that date. After the system comes back, open e-Tax My Page, check the notice-receipt method, and review the NTA exception list for the specific notice you care about.
common_costly_mistakes: Assuming a past electronic-delivery choice automatically carries forward to every future notice.
Assuming every notice requires the new blanket-consent setting; refund notices and some certificates follow separate rules.
Trying to use e-Tax during the September 19–24 maintenance window and leaving a time-sensitive filing until the outage.
Ignoring paper mail because you expected everything to remain electronic.
content.uncertainty: High confidence on the September 24 change, the general re-consent rule and the listed exceptions because they are stated by the National Tax Agency. The NTA also says detailed instructions for the new blanket-consent procedure will be announced separately, so exact screen steps may still change.

30_sec: From September 24, e-Tax changes electronic-notice consent from mostly per-filing choices to a My Page blanket setting.
Even previous electronic-delivery users may need to choose electronic delivery again.
There are exceptions, including refund notices, tax certificates, some mortgage-deduction certificates and invoice-registration notices.
e-Tax is also scheduled to be down September 19 through the morning of September 24, plus September 26.
reading_levels.2_min: This is easy to miss because it is not a tax-rate change. From September 24, 2026, Japan’s e-Tax expands electronic delivery of tax notices and changes the consent model. In principle, users who want electronic delivery will use a blanket setting in My Page instead of repeatedly opting in on individual filings. The National Tax Agency says even people who previously used electronic delivery may need this new setting. However, the transition is not uniform: refund notices still depend on the choice made on the refund filing, electronically requested certificates continue separately, and some mortgage-deduction and invoice-registration notices can rely on earlier consent. The practical move is to verify your My Page setting after September 24 and not assume every notice follows the same rule.

action_plan.goal: Keep e-Tax notice delivery aligned with your preference after the September system change.
action_plan.who_should_act: Anyone who uses e-Tax and expects important tax-office notices electronically.
action_plan.deadline: Check after September 24, 2026; no universal statutory deadline is created by the setting change itself.
prepare: My Number card or other authentication needed to view protected messages
A note of which tax notices you currently receive electronically

steps.action: Do not leave a necessary e-Tax submission until the September 19–24 maintenance period.
steps.how: Submit before the outage when practical or wait until service resumes if your legal deadline allows.
steps.done_when: You have confirmed the maintenance window does not collide with a filing you must make.

steps.action: Open e-Tax My Page and check the new notice-receipt setting.
steps.how: Select electronic delivery if that is your preference, then confirm whether your specific notice falls under a transition exception.
steps.done_when: Your My Page receipt method matches your preference and you understand any notice-specific exception.

mistakes_to_avoid: Treating the transition as a tax increase or new filing obligation.
Assuming old per-filing consent controls all notices after September 24.
Assuming the new blanket setting controls refund notices in the same way.
Discarding paper tax-office mail during the transition.
